registered_predictions.R1_fold_is_an_expansion: ARITHMETIC, stated first because it frames everything: the folded object is 4 x (V x hd) x H = 4.19M numbers, 3.1x the whole 1.34M-parameter model and 4x the embedding it is derived from, because the fold trades 4 x 128 x 128 = 65k weights for a V-row table. So a description that STORES the fold cannot beat the model unless the fold is coded below 2.10 Mbit (the four projection matrices it replaces). Prediction: no dictionary point below 2.10 Mbit is within 0.10 nats of the model, so Description A LOSES as a description while still being the right object for the method test.
registered_predictions.R2_objective_ports: The context-expected OV objective will beat plain MSE at matched bits at the LOW end of the budget range (the parent's crossover was ~12% of raw bits), by >=15% of the CE gap to the model.
registered_predictions.R3_grouping_flips_with_vocabulary: The parent's per-head-branch grouping (rows of dim 2*hd) will be DOMINATED here by a joint dictionary over the token's whole folded signature, because the index+coefficient cost per row is amortised over 2*hd=32 numbers instead of 256 at V=50304; per-head-branch structure was a quality finding at their scale and is a bits finding at ours.
registered_predictions.R4_anchors_port: Exact anchor rows for the top-B tokens by attribution plus a dictionary tail will beat the pure dictionary at matched bits somewhere on the curve, by >=1.3x in bits at matched CE. This is a RETEST: the earlier negative in FINDING 12 was measured against the embedding table with no context objective.
registered_predictions.R5_nothing_beats_the_model_CE: No point of Description A reaches the model's own held CE (4.7114). If any does it will be at the high-bit end and will be a regularisation effect, not compression.
registered_predictions.R6_quantisation_still_wins_the_bits: As a FULL description, every Description-A point is dominated by the existing quantisation frontier (7.59 Mbit at KL 0.004), because the fold is an expansion.
